# libreac / fuzz_knock

libreac's own fuzz target `fuzz_knock` ([source](source/fuzz_knock.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libreac 1.9.0 (FreeREAC/libreac at d16f3f4e).

Drives the knock, reac_knock, the check that a wire carries no master before libreac drives it: from the payload, a start time and up to 4096 events, each advancing a monotonic clock and saying whether a frame was heard and whether the caller steps the knock. Neither the target nor the library code it runs allocates memory.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libreac.a of every src/*.c of libreac 1.9.0 at commit d16f3f4e, compiled with each build's flags, as libreac's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- init starts a knock that listens, has no licence, and opened at the start time ([lines 59-68](source/fuzz_knock.c#L59-L68)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A step answers NONE or DRIVE; DRIVE comes at most once and with the licence set, and only at least REAC_KNOCK_LISTEN_NS after the wire came up and after the last frame heard ([lines 87-113](source/fuzz_knock.c#L87-L113)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The licence is not withheld: a step at or after that time, with nothing heard since and no licence yet granted, drives ([lines 115-129](source/fuzz_knock.c#L115-L129)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- granted is set exactly when DRIVE has come, and a later frame does not revoke it; the state is PROVEN after DRIVE, else CANCELLED after a frame, else LISTENING ([lines 131-154](source/fuzz_knock.c#L131-L154)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libreac` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_knock.plain` | 43,480 | `ca9a1031223344528f79f898eb4fc23e648bba08ce95d95d9aef8b3c250c96bf` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_knock.ubsan` | 43,592 | `edcc54d2e7ee66e28ccc0cf8fb297b9d0dfaa1486f9d044d586de739892a3738` |
| asan | `fuzz_knock.asan` | 558,152 | `61768cf4739b7641c99c825dde45eddafc55b601d41109555be0272fc7ca4118` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_knock.asan-ubsan` | 558,224 | `f834165f5002e65398e68d514ab2a5a5b10e53144f0b41b93ebbc6f895290e82` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
